intent: Record as reviewed the redistribution, curation, fork, purge, operator note and content rules the registry Context enforces and tests.
observable_outcome: get-context registry lists the rules as reviewed, each proven by its test.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Releasing a skill for redistribution is refused when the claimed licence differs from the one its newest version records, and the stored value is unchanged.
A generated skill's redistribution can be neither blocked nor allowed; it stays generated.
Curating a skill is refused when it is not in a catalogue Workspace, and its tier is unchanged.
Withdrawing curation is allowed for any skill, inside a catalogue or not, and clears the curated version.
A version of uploaded content cannot be added to a generated skill; it is refused as a name collision and consumes no version number.
Forking a taken-down skill finds nothing.
A fork starts with its source's access restriction, so forking cannot get around a licensing hold.
A purge keeps a source skill while any fork of it stays, transitively down fork chains.
A purge keeps a skill that has test cases or a version referenced by a run, a download or a bundle.
A fork of a fork reuses the base name instead of growing it, treating only an ordinal of two or more as a series number.
An operator note longer than the contract's cap is refused; a note of exactly the cap is accepted.
The operator note cap counts characters, not bytes, so a note of Chinese characters up to the cap is accepted.
Restricting a skill with a reason code outside the known set is refused, listing the known codes.
A taken-down skill's package is never reported as current content.
A version diff finds nothing when a named version belongs to another skill, even in the same Workspace.
A file larger than 1 MiB on either side gets no text diff; exactly 1 MiB is diffed.
